title: Washington AI Laws

reading.body:
Washington's only AI law regulates companion chatbots, not the data centers or power that constrain AI scaling.

HB2225, passed March 24, 2026, targets a narrow consumer application. It requires operators to disclose that a chatbot is artificial and not human, with recurring notifications. It adds protections for minors, restricting sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques. It requires protocols for detecting suicidal ideation or self-harm and public disclosure of those protocols.

The pattern is disclosure and duty of care, aimed at the point where a model talks directly to a person. That is a different layer of the stack from compute. Nothing here touches siting, interconnection, electricity supply, or the physical buildout that limits how much AI can be trained and served. A reader looking for Washington's posture on the grid as the binding constraint will not find it in this law.

One law is a thin basis for characterizing a state. The data covers enacted text only, so it says nothing about bills that failed, pending proposals, or agency rules. It also does not say how the law is enforced or what penalties attach, because those details are not in the enrolled summary given here.

Washington has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Washington

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB2225: Revised for 1st substitute: Regulating artificial intelligence companion chatbots. passed 2026-03-24

    The act regulates AI companion chatbots by requiring operators to disclose that the chatbot is artificial and not human, with recurring notifications. It imposes additional protections for minors, including restrictions on sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques. It also requires operators to maintain protocols for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm and to publicly disclose those protocols.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Washington. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
